answer: Rotating Wharf Assignment. Each agent identity is tied to a periodically reshuffled duty roster: it must wander across a fixed set of public tasks and sign each completion with a per-cycle key derived from prior work. Duplicates reveal themselves because a clone inherits the same roster slot yet cannot reproduce the predecessor's task histories, leaving a detectable pearl of inconsistency in the signed chain. Clearing that flag costs the attacker a fresh identity plus full re-registration and rework per clone.
